howToApplySteps: Visit the official website of Solapur District Administration at https://solapur.gov.in.
Navigate to Notices / Recruitment section and download the official Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra Application Form along with Parishisht-A and Parishisht-B.
Print the application format and fill all details clearly in neat and legible handwriting without scratch marks or overwriting.
Select your targeted location: Gram Panchayat, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat, or Solapur Municipal Corporation (SMC Zone 1 to 8).

Attach self-attested copies of minimum 2 local residence proofs (Property Tax Receipt, Electricity Bill of last 3 months, Phone Bill, Driving License, Voter ID, Nationalized Bank Passbook, Domicile Certificate, or Passport).
For Solapur Municipal Corporation (SMC) applicants, obtain and attach the residence certificate issued by the concerned SMC Zone Office.
Attach Parishisht-A (Mandal Adhikari Infrastructure Inspection Report) and Parishisht-B (Business Plan & Sustainability Details).
Attach 10th & 12th Marksheets, Degree (if any), Computer certificate, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Nationalized Bank Passbook, and CSC registration certificate (if applicable).
Carry the complete file and submit IN PERSON (समक्ष) at: सेतू संकलन, महसूल शाखा, पहिला मजला, जिल्हाधिकारी कार्यालय, शासकीय दूध डेअरी जवळ, सात रस्ता परिसर, सोलापूर - ४१३००३.
Ensure submission on working days between 11:00 AM and 05:00 PM before 30 September 2026. Obtain official receiving acknowledgment stamp.

faqs.question: How many Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendras are advertised in Solapur district?
faqs.answer: A total of 592 centers are advertised across Solapur district, comprising rural Gram Panchayats, Municipal Councils, Nagar Panchayats, and 32 centers in Solapur Municipal Corporation (SMC) zones.

faqs.question: What is the last date to submit the application form for Solapur ASSK?
faqs.answer: The last date for submitting the application is 30 September 2026 up to 05:00 PM on official working days.

faqs.question: Can I submit the application form online or by post?
faqs.answer: No. As per the official notification, applications must be submitted strictly IN PERSON (समक्ष) at the Collector Office Solapur. Applications sent by post, courier, or any other means will be rejected.

faqs.question: Where should the physical application form be submitted in Solapur?
faqs.answer: The application must be submitted to: सेतू संकलन, महसूल शाखा, पहिला मजला, जिल्हाधिकारी कार्यालय, शासकीय दूध डेअरी जवळ, सात रस्ता परिसर, सोलापूर - ४१३००३.

faqs.question: What is the educational qualification required for Solapur ASSK operator?
faqs.answer: The minimum educational qualification is Higher Secondary School Certificate Examination (12th Pass / HSC). Basic computer literacy (MSCIT or equivalent) is preferred.

faqs.question: What are the residence proof requirements?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be a local resident of the concerned village, town, or SMC Zone. At least two self-attested residence proofs must be submitted (Property tax receipt, Electricity bill of last 3 months, Voter ID, Domicile, DL, Nationalized bank passbook, or Passport).

faqs.question: What special requirement applies to Solapur Municipal Corporation (SMC) zone applicants?
faqs.answer: Applicants for SMC Zones 1 to 8 must obtain and attach a residence certificate from the concerned SMC Zone Office confirming residence in that specific zone.

faqs.question: What are Parishisht-A and Parishisht-B?
faqs.answer: Parishisht-A is the physical infrastructure inspection report by the local Mandal Adhikari, and Parishisht-B is the business plan and sustainability report detailing financial viability and service delivery strategy.

faqs.question: Can multiple members of the same family apply or hold a center?
faqs.answer: No. Only one person per family is eligible to apply for or hold an Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra.

faqs.question: What is the taluka-wise breakdown of 592 centers in Solapur?
faqs.answer: Pandharpur: 77, Akkalkot: 63, Karmala: 62, Barshi: 58, Madha: 55, Malshiras: 52, Sangola: 50, Uttar Solapur: 46 (incl. 32 SMC), Dakshin Solapur & Mandrup: 46, Mohol: 43, and Mangalwedha: 40 (Total: 592 Centers).

faqs.question: Is there any application fee for Solapur ASSK recruitment?
faqs.answer: No application fee is stipulated in the official advertisement.

faqs.question: Where can candidates view updates and the merit list?
faqs.answer: All official notices, scrutiny lists, interview announcements, and selection lists will be published on https://solapur.gov.in.

overview: Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India has officially released the detailed notification for the Junior Engineer Examination, 2026 (Notice No. HQ-C-3019/1/2026-C-3). The commission is conducting an open competitive examination for direct recruitment to 1,748 tentative vacancies for the posts of Junior Engineer (Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Telecommunication) across key central government ministries and departments, along with Scientific Assistant in India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Participating departments and organizations in this recruitment drive include Border Roads Organization (BRO), Central Public Works Department (CPWD), Military Engineer Services (MES), Central Water Commission (CWC), Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS), DGQA-NAVAL (Ministry of Defence), Farakka Barrage Project (Ministry of Jal Shakti), Brahmaputra Board, National Technical Research Organization (NTRO), Directorate General of Lighthouses & Lightships (DGLL), Department of Telecommunication (DoT), India Meteorological Department (IMD), and Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying.

All notified posts are classified as Group 'B' Non-Gazetted in Pay Level-6 (₹35,400 to ₹1,12,400/-) of the 7th Central Pay Commission Pay Matrix. Appointed candidates will receive a starting basic pay of ₹35,400/- per month along with admissible central government allowances including Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), and NPS retirement benefits, providing an approximate starting gross salary of ₹56,000/- to ₹68,000/- per month depending on the city of posting.

Selection is conducted through a two-stage Computer Based Examination: Paper-I (Screening/Qualifying in nature, 200 Questions / 200 Marks) and Paper-II (Core Technical Domain, 100 Questions / 300 Marks, which exclusively determines the final merit order), followed by Online Option Preference submission, First Round of Tentative Allocation (FRTA) under sliding mechanism, Document Verification by user departments, and Physical Efficiency Tests (PET) for Border Roads Organization. Eligible candidates can submit their online applications at https://ssc.gov.in between 02 September 2026 and 22 September 2026 (23:00 hours).

For posts with an age limit up to 32 years (CPWD & DGLL), candidates must have been born not earlier than 02 August 1994 and not later than 01 August 2008.

examCentres.details: Examination Centres are spread across all 9 SSC Administrative Regional Jurisdictions: Central Region (CR: Patna, Prayagraj, Agra, Bareilly, Gorakhpur, Kanpur, Lucknow, Meerut, Varanasi, etc.), Eastern Region (ER: Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Ranchi, Dhanbad, Jamshedpur, Cuttack, Siliguri, Gangtok, etc.), KKR (Bengaluru, Mangalore, Mysuru, Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Kozhikode, Thrissur, etc.), MPR (Bhopal, Gwalior, Indore, Jabalpur, Raipur, Bilaspur, etc.), NER (Guwahati, Shillong, Agartala, Imphal, Itanagar, Aizawl, Dimapur), Northern Region (NR: Delhi NCR, Jaipur, Bikaner, Udaipur, Dehradun, Roorkee, Haldwani), North Western Region (NWR: Chandigarh, Shimla, Jammu, Srinagar, Amritsar, Jalandhar, Patiala, Ludhiana), Southern Region (SR: Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli, Hyderabad, Warangal, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Kurnool), and Western Region (WR: Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, Nashik, Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Panaji). Candidates must give preference for 3 centres within the same regional jurisdiction.

selectionProcess: Stage 1: Paper-I (Computer Based Examination - CBE) – 200 Questions, 200 Marks (Duration: 2 Hours). Objective multiple-choice screening examination testing Reasoning (50 Qs), General Awareness (50 Qs), and Core General Engineering (100 Qs). Paper-I is qualifying in nature with negative marking of 0.25 marks per incorrect answer. Shortlisting for Paper-II is based on normalized Paper-I marks.

Stage 2: Paper-II (Computer Based Examination - CBE) – 100 Technical Domain Questions, 300 Marks (Duration: 2 Hours). In-depth technical discipline paper carrying 3 marks per question with 1 mark negative marking. On-screen scientific calculator and virtual IS 456:2000 / Steam tables provided on computer console. Normalized score in Paper-II exclusively determines the final merit position!

Stage 3: Online Post & Department Preference Form – Candidates submit their preference order for various posts and departments via the Online Option Form on ssc.gov.in prior to the declaration of First Round of Tentative Allocation (FRTA).
Stage 4: First Round of Tentative Allocation (FRTA) / Merit List – Published under SSC's sliding mechanism based strictly on Paper-II normalized score and candidate preference.
Stage 5: Document Verification (DV) – Conducted directly by the indented User Ministries / Departments / Organizations before final appointment.

Stage 6: Physical Efficiency Test (PET) & Medical Examination – Mandatory 1-Mile run in 10 minutes and detailed medical standards evaluation at GREF Centre, Pune for candidates selected in Border Roads Organization (BRO).

sections.name: Paper-I: (i) General Intelligence & Reasoning (Compulsory for All)
Paper-I: (iii) General Engineering – Part-A Civil / Part-B Electrical / Part-C Mechanical / Part-D,E,F IMD / Part-G Telecom
Paper-II: Domain Core Technical Paper (Part-A Civil & Structural / Part-B Electrical / Part-C Mechanical / Part-D,E,F IMD / Part-G Telecom) [Virtual Calculator Allowed]

syllabus.section: Paper-I: General Intelligence & Reasoning (50 Marks)
topics: Analogies, similarities and differences, space visualization, problem solving, analysis, judgment, decision making, visual memory, discrimination, observation
Relationship concepts, arithmetical reasoning, verbal and figure classification, arithmetical number series
Abstract ideas and symbols and their relationships, arithmetical computations, and other analytical functions

syllabus.section: Paper-I: General Awareness (50 Marks)
topics: Current events and matters of everyday observation and experience in their scientific aspect
History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General Polity, and Scientific Research relating to India and neighboring countries

syllabus.section: Paper-I & II: Part-A (Civil & Structural Engineering)
topics: Engineering Mechanics: System of forces, free-body diagrams, equilibrium equations, internal forces in structures, friction, centre of mass, moment of inertia
Solid Mechanics: Bending moment and shear force in statically determinate beams, stress-strain relationships, flexural and shear stresses, uniform torsion, buckling of columns
Structural Analysis: Statically determinate and indeterminate structures, superposition, trusses, arches, beams, cables and frames, slope deflection, moment distribution, influence lines
Construction Materials & Management: Bricks, stones, timber, steel, cement, aggregates, plastics, polymers, glass, concrete mix design, testing; PERT & CPM network analysis
Estimating, Costing & Valuation: Fundamentals of estimating, cost estimates, rate analysis, valuation, detailed estimates
Concrete Structures: Working stress & limit state design, beams, slabs, columns, foundation, retaining walls, bond and development length
Steel Structures: Bolted connections, welds, tension and compression members, beams, plastic analysis
Surveying: Principles, errors, maps, chain & compass, plane table, levelling, traversing, triangulation, total station, tacheometric and theodolite surveying
Soil Mechanics: Phase relationships, index properties, soil classification, permeability, seepage, flow nets, effective stress, compaction, consolidation, shear strength, Mohr's circle
Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulics: Fluid statics, continuity, momentum and energy equations, laminar and turbulent flow, pipe networks, channel hydraulics, specific energy, hydraulic jump
Hydrology & Irrigation: Hydrologic cycle, precipitation, runoff, unit hydrographs, flood routing, groundwater hydraulics, Darcy's law; irrigation methods, duty, delta, dams, spillways, canals
Water & Wastewater Quality & Treatment: Standards, WQI, treatment unit processes, distribution, sewerage system design, effluent discharge standards, sludge disposal
Transportation & Traffic Engineering: Highway geometric design, railway track speed and cant, pavement materials and IRC design, traffic flow and speed studies, signal design by Webster's method

syllabus.section: Paper-I & II: Part-B (Electrical Engineering)
topics: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering: Circuit elements (R, L, C, Batteries), voltage, current, power, energy, flux and units; KCL, KVL, node and mesh analysis
Network Theorems: Thevenin's, Norton's, Superposition, Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
Magnetic Circuits: Reluctance, self and mutual inductance, magnetomotive force (MMF)
A.C. Fundamentals: RMS and average values, resonance, balanced three-phase circuits, star-delta transformation, complex power and power factor
Measurement & Instruments: Ammeter, voltmeter, wattmeter, Wheatstone and Kelvin bridges, energy meter, megger, CT, PT, calibration of electronic energy meter
Electrical Machines: Single-phase and three-phase transformers; DC machines (types, characteristics, losses, efficiency); AC induction motors (starting, braking, speed control, torque-speed curves)
Synchronous Machines: Fractional motors, servomotors, armature reaction, parallel operation, synchronization
Generation, Transmission & Distribution: Power stations, load factor, diversity factor, transmission line parameters, corona and Ferranti effect, circuit breakers, protective relays, coaxial cables
Estimation & Costing: Lighting schemes, electrical installation of machines, earthing practices, Indian Electricity (IE) Rules

Utilization & Power Electronics: Illumination, electric heating, electric welding, electroplating, electric traction; diodes, BJT, FET, thyristor V-I characteristics, firing circuits, DC-DC buck/boost converters, rectifiers

syllabus.section: Paper-I & II: Part-C (Mechanical Engineering)
topics: Engineering Mechanics & Strength of Materials: Free-body diagrams, equilibrium, Lami's theorem, friction, centroid; simple stress-strain, shear force and bending moment, beam deflection, torsion, thin cylinders

Theory of Machines & Machine Design: Cams and followers, gears, belts, chains, flywheels, governors, balancing, vibrations, brakes, clutches, bearings; creep and fatigue, failure theories, cotter/knuckle joints, shafts, couplings, springs, fasteners
Materials Science & Engineering: Crystal structures, iron-carbon phase diagram, heat treatment of steel, cast iron, non-ferrous alloys, NDT, corrosion

Thermal Engineering: Laws of thermodynamics, cycles (Otto, Diesel, Dual, Rankine, Brayton), steam generators, boilers, impulse and reaction turbines, cooling towers, IC engines, compressors, refrigeration and air conditioning, heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation)
Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulic Machinery: Fluid properties, continuity equation, jet impact, hydraulic turbines, centrifugal and reciprocating pumps

Manufacturing Engineering: Pattern making, casting, welding (gas, arc, resistance), lathe, milling, grinding, press working; metrology (linear/angular, CMM, limits, fits, tolerances); CNC milling, EDM, ECM, AJM, robotics, FMS
Industrial Engineering: Plant layout, work study, PPC, statistical quality control, inventory control

syllabus.section: Paper-I & II: Part-D, E, F & G (IMD & Telecom Subjects)
topics: Part-D (Computer Science & IT - IMD): Discrete maths, linear algebra, digital logic, computer architecture, C programming & data structures, algorithms, theory of computation, compiler design, OS, databases (ER model, SQL, transactions), computer networks (OSI, TCP/IP, routing)

Part-E (Electronics & Telecommunication - IMD): Semiconductors, diodes, BJT/FET/MOSFET, amplifiers, network theorems, digital electronics, sequential logic; antennas, propagation, modulation (AM/FM/PM/SSB), multiplexing (FDM/TDM), fiber optics

Part-F (Physics - IMD): Mathematical physics, mechanics, properties of matter, oscillations and waves, optics and interference, electricity and magnetism, kinetic theory and thermodynamics, modern physics, solid state physics, semiconductor devices

Part-G (Telecommunication Engineering - DoT): Engineering mathematics, network analysis, signals & systems (continuous/discrete, LTI), semiconductor devices, analog/digital circuits, control systems, analog and digital communications, electromagnetics & transmission lines

howToApply: Step 1: One-Time Registration (OTR) – Visit the official Staff Selection Commission portal at https://ssc.gov.in or download the 'mySSC' mobile application from Google Play Store. If you have not created an OTR on the new website (earlier OTR from ssc.nic.in is invalid), click on 'Register Now' under Login/Register.

Step 2: Complete Personal & Education Details – Enter your name, father's name, mother's name, and date of birth strictly as recorded in your Class 10th Matriculation certificate. Provide board name, roll number, year of passing, active mobile number, and email ID (verified via OTP).

Step 3: Choose Aadhaar Authentication – Candidates are advised to authenticate using Aadhaar during OTR to enjoy exemptions from photo/signature technical rejection rules and streamlined entry at exam venues.

Step 4: Login & Access Live Examination – Log into ssc.gov.in using your Registration Number and Password. Navigate to the 'Live Examination' tab and click 'Apply' under 'Junior Engineer Examination, 2026'.

Step 5: Post Selection & Exam Subject – Choose the posts for which you are eligible based on your Degree/Diploma engineering stream. Select the examination subject (Civil Part-A, Electrical Part-B, Mechanical Part-C, CS/IT Part-D, ECE Part-E, Physics Part-F, or Telecom Part-G).

Step 6: Capture Real-Time Live Photo – The application captures your live photograph via webcam or through the 'mySSC' mobile app using a QR code. Ensure plain background, eye-level camera, good lighting, and no spectacles, caps, or masks.
Step 7: Upload Scanned Signature – Upload your signature in JPEG format (10 to 20 KB, dimensions 6.0 cm width x 2.0 cm height).
Step 8: Select Examination Centres – Select three preferred examination centres in order of priority within the same SSC Regional Jurisdiction.
Step 9: Preview & Submit Form – Thoroughly review all entered details in the preview window. Accept the declaration by clicking 'I Agree', enter the Captcha code, and click 'Submit'.

Step 10: Fee Payment & Print Application – Pay the application fee of ₹100/- via BHIM UPI, Net Banking, or Debit Card (Women, SC, ST, PwBD, ESM are exempt). Print the final application confirmation slip for your records.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies are announced for SSC Junior Engineer Examination 2026?
faqs.answer: A total of 1,748 tentative vacancies have been announced across 14 central government organizations including BRO, CPWD, MES, CWC, CWPRS, DGQA-Naval, NTRO, DGLL, DoT, IMD, and Ministry of Fisheries. Post-wise and category-wise details are published on ssc.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the official advertisement number and online application deadline for SSC JE 2026?
faqs.answer: The official notification file number is F. No. HQ-C-3019/1/2026-C-3 published on 02 September 2026. The online application window is open from 02 September 2026 to 22 September 2026 (23:00 hours). The fee payment deadline is 23 September 2026 (23:00 hours).

faqs.question: What is the pay scale and starting salary for SSC Junior Engineer posts?
faqs.answer: All Junior Engineer posts and Scientific Assistant (IMD) are Group 'B' Non-Gazetted posts in Level-6 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (₹35,400 – ₹1,12,400/-) with initial basic pay of ₹35,400/- per month. Gross monthly salary ranges from approx. ₹56,000/- to ₹68,000/- per month including DA, HRA, and Transport Allowance.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and crucial reckoning date for SSC JE 2026?
faqs.answer: The crucial date for age reckoning is 01 August 2026. For posts with an age limit up to 30 years, candidates must be born between 02 August 1996 and 01 August 2008. For CPWD and DGLL posts (up to 32 years), candidates must be born between 02 August 1994 and 01 August 2008. Standard age relaxations apply for SC/ST (5 yrs), OBC (3 yrs), and PwBD (10-15 yrs).

faqs.question: Is work experience mandatory for all SSC JE posts?
faqs.answer: No. Degree holders (B.E. / B.Tech) require NO experience for any post. Experience is only required for Diploma holders applying to Border Roads Organization (BRO - 2 years), Military Engineer Services (MES - 2 years), DGQA-Naval (2 years), and DGLL (3 years). For CPWD, CWC, CWPRS, NTRO, DoT, IMD, and Fisheries, fresh Diploma and Degree holders can apply without experience.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and marking scheme for SSC JE CBE?
faqs.answer: Paper-I has 200 objective MCQs (Reasoning: 50, GA: 50, Engineering Domain: 100) for 200 marks in 2 hours with 0.25 negative marking. Paper-II has 100 core domain questions for 300 marks in 2 hours with 1.00 negative marking. An on-screen virtual scientific calculator and IS code tables are enabled in Paper-II.

faqs.question: Are Paper-I marks included in the final merit list?
faqs.answer: No. Paper-I is qualifying in nature and is used strictly to shortlist candidates for Paper-II. Final merit ranking and post allocation are prepared exclusively based on normalized marks obtained in Paper-II (300 Marks).

faqs.question: What are the special physical standards and PET for Border Roads Organization (BRO)?
faqs.answer: Only MALE candidates are eligible for BRO. Candidates must qualify the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) consisting of a 1-Mile run in 10 minutes at GREF Centre, Pune. Minimum height criteria range from 152 cm to 162.5 cm depending on the candidate's home region/state.

faqs.question: What is the application fee and who is exempted?
faqs.answer: The application fee is ₹100/- for General, OBC, and EWS male candidates. All Women candidates, SC, ST, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen (ESM) candidates are completely exempt from payment of any application fee.

faqs.question: When can candidates make corrections in their submitted application form?
faqs.answer: The 'Window for Online Application Form Correction' will be open from 28 September 2026 to 30 September 2026 (23:00 hours). Candidates can correct their form up to two times with correction charges of ₹200/- for the 1st correction and ₹500/- for the 2nd correction.

overview: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has officially published Examination Notice No. 01/2027-GEOL (File No. 04/01/2026-E.I(B)) for the Combined Geo-Scientist Examination, 2027 (CGSE 2027). This nationwide prestigious competitive examination is conducted for direct recruitment to 127 Group 'A' and Group 'B' gazetted scientific positions in the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Ministry of Mines, and the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti.

The 127 notified vacancies are divided into two distinct categories: Category-I features 111 posts in GSI including Geologist Group 'A' (29 posts), Chemist Group 'A' (07 posts), Assistant Geologist Group 'B' (34 posts), Assistant Geophysicist Group 'B' (35 posts), and Assistant Chemist Group 'B' (06 posts). Category-II features 16 posts in CGWB including Scientist 'B' (Hydrogeology) Group 'A' (05 posts), Scientist 'B' (Chemical) Group 'A' (01 post), Scientist 'B' (Geophysics) Group 'A' (01 post), Assistant Hydrogeologist Group 'B' (07 posts), Assistant Chemist Group 'B' (01 post), and Assistant Geophysicist Group 'B' (01 post).

Appointed officers in Group 'A' posts are placed in Level-10 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (₹56,100 – ₹1,77,500/-) with starting basic pay of ₹56,100/- per month (gross monthly salary approx ₹90,000 – ₹1,10,000/-), while Group 'B' officers are placed in Level-8 of the Pay Matrix (₹47,600 – ₹1,51,100/-) with starting basic pay of ₹47,600/- per month (gross monthly salary approx ₹75,000 – ₹90,000/-), along with central government DA, HRA, Transport Allowance, and official perks.

The examination follows a rigorous three-tier selection process: Stage-I Preliminary Examination (Objective type on OMR Sheet, 400 Marks, scheduled for 10 January 2027), Stage-II Main Examination (Conventional/Descriptive type, 600 Marks, scheduled for 19 & 20 June 2027), and Stage-III Personality Test / Interview (200 Marks). Crucially, marks from ALL THREE stages (Stage-I + Stage-II + Stage-III = 1,200 Total Marks) are counted towards the final merit order and service allocation. Eligible postgraduates must submit their online applications via the UPSC portal at https://upsconline.nic.in on or before 22 September 2026 (till 18:00 Hours).

examCentres.details: Stage-I Preliminary Examination will be held across 21 Centres: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Chennai, Cuttack, Delhi, Dispur, Ghaziabad, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Patna, Prayagraj (Allahabad), Shillong, Shimla, and Thiruvananthapuram. (Allotted on First-Apply-First-Allot basis with capacity ceilings, except Chennai, Dispur, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad). Stage-II Main Examination will be held at 9 Centres: Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, and Shimla.

selectionProcess: Stage-I: Combined Geo-Scientist (Preliminary) Examination – Objective type on OMR Sheet comprising two papers (Paper-I: General Studies, 100 Marks; Paper-II: Stream Specific Discipline, 300 Marks; Total 400 Marks, 2 Hours each). Negative marking: 1/3rd (0.33) marks per wrong answer. Marks scored in Stage-I ARE COUNTED towards the final merit order! Candidates shortlisted for Main Exam at 6 to 7 times the number of vacancies.

Stage-II: Combined Geo-Scientist (Main) Examination – Conventional / Descriptive type examination consisting of three papers for each stream (3 Hours & 200 Marks each, Total 600 Marks). Answers must be written in English only. Non-programmable pocket calculators permitted. Marks scored in Stage-II ARE COUNTED towards the final merit order!

Stage-III: Personality Test / Interview – Carrying 200 Marks with no minimum qualifying marks. Candidates obtaining qualifying marks in Stage-II will be summoned for Interview in a ratio of approx. twice (2x) the number of vacancies to assess leadership, field life aptitude, intellectual curiosity, and integrity.

Final Merit Order & Service Allocation: Prepared strictly on the basis of aggregate marks secured in all three stages combined: Stage-I (400 Marks) + Stage-II (600 Marks) + Stage-III (200 Marks) = Grand Total 1,200 Marks, subject to verification of eligibility and order of service preferences.

syllabus.section: Stage-I Preliminary: Paper-I General Studies (Common for All Streams - 100 Marks)
topics: Current events of national and international importance
History of India and Indian National Movement
Indian and World Geography - Physical, Social, Economic Geography of India and the World
Indian Polity and Governance - Constitution, Political System, Panchayati Raj, Public Policy, Rights Issues etc.
Economic and Social Development - Sustainable Development, Poverty, Inclusion, Demographics, Social Sector initiatives etc.
General issues on Environmental Ecology, Bio-diversity and Climate Change - that do not require subject specialisation
General Science

syllabus.section: Stage-I Preliminary: Paper-II Geology / Hydrogeology (300 Marks)
topics: Physical Geology: Principle of uniformitarianism; origin, differentiation and internal structure of Earth; origin of atmosphere; earthquakes and volcanoes; continental drift, sea-floor spreading, isostasy, orogeny and plate tectonics; geological action of rivers, wind, glaciers, waves; landforms; weathering processes

Structural Geology: Stress, strain and rheological properties of rocks; planar and linear structures; folds and faults; Mohr's circle and failure criteria; ductile and brittle shear; toposheets, V-rules, outcrop patterns, stereographic projections

Mineralogy: Symmetry, notations, indices; Bravais lattices; chemical classification; isomorphism, polymorphism, solid solution; silicate structures; physical and optical properties of rock forming minerals (olivine, garnet, pyroxene, amphibole, mica, feldspar, quartz)

Igneous Petrology: Magma types and evolution; IUGS classification; textures and structures; binary and ternary phase diagrams; magmatic differentiation and assimilation; petrogenesis of granites, basalts, komatiites, alkaline rocks
Metamorphic Petrology: Controls of metamorphism; slate, schist, gneiss; metamorphic textures; zones, isograds, facies; geothermal gradients and plate tectonics
Sedimentology: Origin, textures, grain-size scale; primary sedimentary structures; sandstone and carbonate classification; siliciclastic depositional environments and facies; diagenesis

Paleontology: Fossilization; species concept; morphology and classification of invertebrates (Trilobites, Brachiopods, Lamellibranchs, Gastropods, Cephalopods); evolution in Equidae and Hominidae; microfossils (Foraminifera, Ostracoda); Gondwana flora

Stratigraphy: Superposition; litho-, bio-, and chronostratigraphy; Archaean cratons (Dharwar, Singhbhum, Aravalli); Proterozoic mobile belts; Purana basins (Cuddapah, Vindhyan); Phanerozoic stratigraphy of India; Siwaliks; Indo-Gangetic alluvium

Economic Geology: Mineral deposit properties, form, assemblage, texture; magmatic, pegmatitic, hydrothermal, supergene, metamorphic ore formation; coal and petroleum formation; major Indian mineral and hydrocarbon deposits
Hydrogeology: Aquifer characteristics, porosity, permeability, transmissivity; Darcy's Law; Bernoulli equation; groundwater composition; H and O isotopes; artificial recharge

syllabus.section: Stage-I Preliminary: Paper-II Geophysics (300 Marks)
topics: Solid Earth Geophysics: Origin and characteristics of planets; Earth's shape, rotation, gravity and magnetic fields; Geomagnetism, rock magnetism; Elastic waves, internal structure of Earth; Plate tectonics, earthquakes, focal depth, intensity and magnitude scales

Mathematical Methods in Geophysics: Vector analysis, Gauss's and Stoke's theorems; Matrices, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Newton's law of gravitation; Conservation laws; Rigid body motion; Inverse theory, forward and inverse problems; Numerical methods, differential equations

Electromagnetism: Electrostatic and magneto-static fields; Coulomb's, Ampere's, Biot-Savart's, Gauss's laws; Laplace's and Poisson's equations; Maxwell's equations; Electromagnetic vector and scalar potentials

Geophysical Prospecting: Gravity, magnetic, electrical, electromagnetic, and well-logging methods; Seismic reflection and refraction; Fermat's principle, Snell's law; Signal processing, Fourier transform, sampling theorem, convolution
Remote Sensing & Thermodynamics: EM spectrum, Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien's laws, sensor interactions; Laws of thermodynamics and thermodynamic potentials
Nuclear Physics & Radiometry: Radioactivity, decay laws, radioactive minerals; Radiation detectors (GM counter, scintillation counter, gamma-ray spectrometer); Wave-particle duality

syllabus.section: Stage-I Preliminary: Paper-II Chemistry (300 Marks)
topics: Chemical Periodicity: Schrödinger equation, radial distribution curves; Modern IUPAC Periodic table, trends in radii, ionization enthalpy, electron affinity, electronegativity; Oxidation states and redox chemistry

Chemical Bonding & Structure: Ionic bonding, lattice energy, Born-Haber cycle; Covalent bonding, VBT, MOT, hybridization, resonance; Coordinate bonding, Werner theory, chelate complexes, isomerism in square planar and octahedral complexes
Acids and Bases: Chemical and ionic equilibrium, Ostwald dilution law, pH scale, buffer action, Henderson equation
Quantitative Inorganic Analysis: Volumetric analysis, standard solutions; Acid-base, redox, complexometric, and precipitation titrations; Indicators
Kinetic Theory & Gaseous State: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, collision diameter, mean free path, effusion rates
Chemical Thermodynamics & Equilibrium: First and second laws, state functions, Joule-Thomson coefficient; Gibbs and Helmholtz functions; Criteria for spontaneity
Solutions of Non-Electrolytes: Raoult's law, colligative properties, osmosis, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point
Electrochemistry: Cell constant, Kohlrausch's law, ionic mobility, Debye-Hückel theory, conductometric titrations, transport numbers
Basic Organic Chemistry: Resonance, hyperconjugation, reactive intermediates (carbocations, carbanions, free radicals)

Stereochemistry & Reaction Mechanisms: Chirality, R/S nomenclature, E/Z naming; Aliphatic substitutions (SN1, SN2); Eliminations (E1, E2, Saytzeff/Hoffman); Additions; Electrophilic aromatic substitutions; Molecular rearrangements

syllabus.section: Stage-II Main: Geology Papers I, II & III (Descriptive - 600 Marks)
topics: Geology Paper-I: Physical geology and remote sensing (geomorphic landforms, digital image processing, LANDSAT/IRS); Structural geology (stress-strain, ductile/brittle shear, microfabrics); Sedimentology (fluid/sediment flows, sequence stratigraphy); Paleontology (fossil record, mass extinctions); Stratigraphy (Precambrian cratons, Phanerozoic basins)

Geology Paper-II: Mineralogy (crystal classes, optical properties, rock-forming minerals); Geochemistry and isotope geology (radiometric dating, REE patterns, stable isotopes); Igneous petrology (magmatic crystallization, phase diagrams, mantle melting); Metamorphic petrology (P-T-t paths, metamorphic facies, thermodynamics); Geodynamics (seismic discontinuities, paleomagnetism, mantle plumes)

Geology Paper-III: Economic geology (ore-forming processes, hydrothermal/magmatic deposits, fluid inclusions); Indian mineral deposits and mineral economics (National Mineral Policy, strategic minerals); Mineral exploration (geochemical/geophysical surveys, drilling, reserve estimation); Fuel and engineering geology (coalification, petroleum systems, dam/tunnel investigations); Environmental geology and natural hazards

syllabus.section: Stage-II Main: Geophysics Papers I, II & III (Descriptive - 600 Marks)
topics: Geophysics Paper-I: Solid Earth Geophysics; Earthquake Seismology (seismotectonics, focal mechanisms, seismic tomography); Mathematical Methods in Geophysics; Geophysical Inversion (least squares, singular value decomposition, SVD, genetic algorithms); Mathematical Methods of Physics (Green's function, partial differential equations)

Geophysics Paper-II: Electrodynamics; Electromagnetic Theory (waveguides, transmission lines); Atmospheric & Space Physics (ionosphere, GPS); Potential Field (Gravity & Magnetic) Methods; Electrical and Electromagnetic Methods (ERT, IP, MT, GPR); Seismic Prospecting (2D/3D CDP, migration, VSP); Borehole Geophysics (wireline logging); Classical Mechanics; Thermodynamics & Statistical Physics; Atomic/Molecular Physics; Nuclear Physics

Geophysics Paper-III: Radiometric & Airborne Geophysics; Marine Geophysics; Geophysical Signal Processing (FFT, digital filtering, deconvolution); Remote Sensing & Geohydrology; Solid State Physics & Electronics; Laser Systems; Digital Electronics, Radar & Satellite Communications; Quantum Mechanics (Schrodinger equation, perturbation theory)

syllabus.section: Stage-II Main: Chemistry Papers I, II & III (Descriptive - 600 Marks)
topics: Chemistry Paper-I (Inorganic): Inorganic solids (defects, zeolites, superconductors); Coordination compounds (Crystal Field Theory, ligand field stabilization, spectrochemical series); Acid-base, gravimetric, and redox titrations; Complexometric titrations (EDTA); Organometallic compounds (18-electron rule, catalysts); Nuclear chemistry; Chemistry of d- and f-block elements

Chemistry Paper-II (Physical): Kinetic theory and real gases (van der Waals, virial equation); Solids and band theory; Chemical thermodynamics and equilibrium (chemical potential, fugacity, Debye-Huckel limiting law); Kinetics and catalysis; Electrochemistry (Nernst equation, potentiometric titrations); Quantum chemistry (operators, particle in a 3D box); Spectroscopy (Rotational, Vibrational, Raman); Photochemistry (Jablonski diagram, quantum yield)

Chemistry Paper-III (Analytical & Organic): Quantitative errors, statistics (Q-test, t-test); Separation methods (HPLC, GLC, TLC, solvent extraction); Spectroscopic instrumentation (AAS, ICP, UV-Vis, IR); Thermal and X-ray methods; Analysis of geological materials and petroleum; Organic intermediates (carbenes, nitrenes); Carbonyl reactions (Aldol, Claisen, Wittig); Electrocyclic reactions (Woodward-Hoffman rules); Spectroscopy of organic compounds (FTIR, 1H/13C NMR, Mass spectrometry)

howToApply: Step 1: Account Creation & Universal Registration Number (URN) – Visit the official UPSC application portal at https://upsconline.nic.in. If you do not have an active account, complete Account Creation and generate your lifetime unique Universal Registration Number (URN).

Step 2: Fill Common Application Form (CAF) – Complete the Common Application Form (CAF) with personal details, educational qualifications, address, and photo identity details (Aadhaar Card is strongly recommended for seamless verification).

Step 3: Capture Live Photograph & Upload Recent Photo – Applicants must upload a clear scanned photograph AND capture a real-time live photograph through the portal webcam module adhering to UPSC photo guidelines.
Step 4: Upload Three-Fold Signature – Sign three times (one below the other) on a plain white paper with black ink and upload the scanned signature image as instructed.

Step 5: Fill Examination Specific Module – Select 'Combined Geo-Scientist Examination, 2027'. Choose your Stream/Discipline (Geology/Hydrogeology, Geophysics, or Chemistry) and indicate service preferences for GSI and CGWB posts.

Step 6: Select Preliminary Examination Centre – Select your preferred Stage-I Preliminary Examination Centre from the list of 21 cities. (Note: Allotted on First-Apply-First-Allot basis; early application is advised).

Step 7: Pay Examination Fee – Pay the fee of ₹200/- online using Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, or UPI (Female, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt). Both GSI and CGWB options require only one common application and single fee payment.

Step 8: Final Submission & Application Number Generation – Verify all details in the preview module, submit the form, and note down the generated Application Number alongside your URN for all future references.

faqs.question: What is the official examination notice number and application deadline for UPSC CGSE 2027?
faqs.answer: The official notification is Examination Notice No. 01/2027-GEOL (File No. 04/01/2026-E.I(B)) released on 02 September 2026. Online applications can be submitted up to 22 September 2026 till 18:00 Hours.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies are announced in UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination 2027?
faqs.answer: A total of 127 vacancies are notified across two categories: 111 vacancies in Geological Survey of India (GSI, Ministry of Mines) and 16 vacancies in Central Ground Water Board (CGWB, Ministry of Jal Shakti).

faqs.question: What are the pay scales for Group 'A' and Group 'B' posts under UPSC CGSE 2027?
faqs.answer: Group 'A' posts (Geologist, Chemist, Scientist 'B') carry Pay Level-10 (₹56,100 – ₹1,77,500/-) with basic pay ₹56,100/-. Group 'B' posts (Assistant Geologist, Assistant Geophysicist, Assistant Chemist, Assistant Hydrogeologist) carry Pay Level-8 (₹47,600 – ₹1,51,100/-) with basic pay ₹47,600/-.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and crucial date for calculating age in UPSC CGSE 2027?
faqs.answer: Candidates must be between 21 and 32 years of age as on 01 January 2027 (born between 02 January 1995 and 01 January 2006). Standard relaxations apply: SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD (10 years), Ex-Servicemen (5 years), and Departmental GSI/CGWB employees (up to 5 years).

faqs.question: Are candidates appearing in their final year of Master's Degree eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates who have appeared or are appearing in the qualifying M.Sc / M.Tech examination can apply provisionally. They must submit proof of passing within 10 days of the declaration of Stage-II Main examination results.

faqs.question: Are Stage-I Preliminary examination marks counted towards the final merit ranking?
faqs.answer: YES! Unlike civil services where prelims is purely screening, in UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination, marks obtained in Stage-I Prelims (400 Marks) ARE COUNTED along with Stage-II Main (600 Marks) and Stage-III Interview (200 Marks) for a combined total of 1,200 Marks to determine final merit and service allocation.

faqs.question: What are the examination dates for Stage-I Prelims and Stage-II Mains?
faqs.answer: The Combined Geo-Scientist (Preliminary) Examination is scheduled for 10 January 2027 (Sunday). The Combined Geo-Scientist (Main) Examination will be conducted on 19 June 2027 & 20 June 2027.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for both GSI and CGWB posts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates eligible for both Category-I (GSI) and Category-II (CGWB) posts within their stream need to fill in only ONE online application form and pay the application fee only once.

faqs.question: What is the application fee and who is exempt?
faqs.answer: The application fee is ₹200/- for General, OBC, and EWS male candidates. All Female candidates, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) are completely exempted from payment of fee.

faqs.question: Are calculators allowed in the examination?
faqs.answer: Calculators are strictly PROHIBITED in Stage-I Preliminary (Objective) Examination. However, battery-operated non-programmable pocket calculators are PERMITTED in Stage-II Main (Conventional Descriptive) Examination.

faqs.question: How many Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendras are to be established in Thane district under this advertisement?
faqs.answer: A total of 381 Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendras (ASSK) are being established across rural Gram Panchayats in 6 talukas of Thane district.

faqs.question: What is the taluka-wise breakdown of 381 ASSK centers in Thane?
faqs.answer: The distribution is: Kalyan - 115 centers, Bhiwandi - 111 centers, Murbad - 76 centers, Shahapur - 48 centers, Ambernath - 27 centers, and Thane - 4 centers.

faqs.question: What is the last date to apply for Thane ASSK recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: The online Google Form must be submitted between 20 August 2026 and 20 September 2026. The physical dossier must be submitted to the respective Taluka Resident Naib Tehsildar by 22 September 2026 (up to 6:15 PM).

faqs.question: What is the educational qualification required for Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra operator?
faqs.answer: The minimum qualification is 12th Pass (Higher Secondary Certificate - HSC). Candidates with basic computer literacy (MSCIT or equivalent) are preferred. Additional marks are awarded for Degree (+2 marks) and Post Graduation (+5 marks).

faqs.question: Is local residency mandatory for applying to a specific Gram Panchayat center?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must strictly be a local resident of the concerned Gram Panchayat area. Proof of local residence issued by the Gram Panchayat must be attached.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for Thane ASSK recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: The applicant must have completed a minimum of 18 years of age. There is no upper age limit specified in the official notification.

faqs.question: How will candidates be evaluated and selected for ASSK?
faqs.answer: Selection is strictly based on a 100-Marks Evaluation Matrix defined by Maharashtra Government Corrigendum dated 09 July 2026, comprising Education (10), Computer Literacy (15), Infrastructure (15), Financial Capacity (10), Interview (20), Experience (10), Business Plan (5), Social Inclusivity (5), and Police Verification (10).

faqs.question: What are the minimum infrastructure requirements for setting up an ASSK center?
faqs.answer: The center must have at least 100 sq. ft. of commercial space, 2 computers/laptops, laser printer, scanner, biometric device, webcam, UPS power backup, broadband internet (10 Mbps rural, 20 Mbps urban), CCTV system, and a citizen waiting area.

faqs.question: Where should the physical application form and documents be submitted?
faqs.answer: The printed form and self-attested documents must be submitted in person to the office of the Resident Naib Tehsildar (निवासी नायब तहसीलदार) of the respective Taluka where the applicant is applying.

faqs.question: Can more than one person from the same family apply or get a center?
faqs.answer: No. As per government rules, only one member per family (husband, wife, unmarried children) is eligible to be granted an Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for Thane ASSK recruitment?
faqs.answer: There is no application fee mentioned in the official advertisement issued by the District Collector Office, Thane.

faqs.question: Who receives preference under the social inclusivity criteria?
faqs.answer: Under government guidelines, 5 marks are reserved for social inclusivity, giving preference to Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwD), Ex-Servicemen, Women, Self-Help Group (SHG) members, and local entrepreneurs.

faqs.question: What is the initial tenure of the VLE contract for ASSK?
faqs.answer: The selected Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE) is initially awarded a contract for 1 year. Renewal for subsequent years depends on performance indicators like transaction volume, citizen satisfaction, and system uptime.

faqs.question: Where can candidates view updates and the final merit list for Thane ASSK?
faqs.answer: All updates, scrutiny notices, interview schedules, and final merit lists will be published on the official district portal https://thane.nic.in.

faqs.answer: A total of 640 centers are officially advertised across Latur district, comprising 599 rural Gram Panchayat centers, 10 Municipal Council/Nagar Panchayat centers, and 31 Latur Municipal Corporation (LMC) ward centers.

faqs.question: What are the application start and closing dates for Latur ASSK Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: Online application opens on 25 August 2026 at 11:00 AM and closes on 15 September 2026 at 05:00 PM through setusamitilatur.in.

faqs.question: What is the application fee and how should it be paid?
faqs.answer: The application fee is Rs. 500/-. As per Clause 30 of the notification, the fee must be paid exclusively via QR Code from the applicant OWN bank account, and the payment receipt must be uploaded with the application.

faqs.question: What is the minimum educational qualification required?
faqs.answer: The minimum qualification is 12th Pass (HSC). Candidates must also possess an MSCIT or CCC computer certificate. Extra marks are given for Degree (+2 marks) and Post-Graduation (+3 marks).

faqs.question: Is local residency mandatory to apply for a center in Latur?
faqs.answer: Yes. The applicant must be a local resident of the specific Gram Panchayat, Municipal Council, or Latur Municipal Corporation Ward applied for, evidenced by a certificate from Gram Sevak, Chief Officer, or Domicile Certificate.

faqs.question: What is the selection process and evaluation matrix?
faqs.answer: Selection is strictly determined by a 100-Marks Evaluation Matrix defined by Maharashtra Govt Corrigendum dated 09 July 2026: Education (10), Computer & Cyber Skills (15), Infrastructure (15), Financial Capacity (10), Interview (20), Experience (10), Business Plan (5), Social Inclusivity (5), and Police Verification (10).

faqs.question: What hardware and office infrastructure is required?
faqs.answer: An independent commercial office of min 100 sq. ft., 2 computers/laptops, laser printer, scanner, biometric scanner, webcam, power backup (UPS), 10-20 Mbps broadband internet, CCTV system, citizen waiting area, and official fee display board.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for multiple centers or multiple family members get a center?
faqs.answer: No. An applicant can apply for only one center within the district. Furthermore, only one person per family (husband, wife, unmarried children) is eligible to be granted an ASSK center.

faqs.question: What is the taluka-wise rural center distribution in Latur?
faqs.answer: Ahmadpur: 60, Ausa: 79, Chakur: 52, Deoni: 35, Jalkot: 19, Latur (Rural): 61, Nilanga: 82, Renapur: 42, Shirur Anantpal: 17, and Udgir: 58 (Total 599 Rural Centers).

faqs.question: What urban centers are available under this notification?
faqs.answer: 10 centers in Municipal Councils (Udgir: 5, Ahmadpur: 2, Nilanga: 1, Renapur: 1, Deoni: 1) and 31 centers across 18 Wards of the Latur City Municipal Corporation.

faqs.question: What happens if no transaction is conducted after being awarded the center?
faqs.answer: As per Clause 15, if a selected center does not conduct a single transaction within 3 consecutive months of approval, the center authorization will be cancelled without prior notice.

faqs.question: Where will updates, scrutiny lists, and merit lists be published?
faqs.answer: All official notices, scrutiny lists, interview schedules, and final selection orders will be published on the official district portal https://latur.gov.in/.

faqs.question: What is the total number of vacancies in MECL Non-Executive Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: A total of 122 vacancies are officially announced under Advertisement No. 03/Rectt./2026 across 16 different posts in Grades W-7, W-4, and W-3.

faqs.question: What are the application start and closing dates for MECL Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: Online registration commences on 12 September 2026 and closes on 11 October 2026 through the official MECL portal.

faqs.question: What is the crucial cut-off date for reckoning age limit, educational qualifications, and experience?
faqs.answer: The crucial cut-off date for calculating age, qualification, and post-qualification experience is 01 September 2026.

faqs.question: What is the upper age limit and are there any category relaxations?
faqs.answer: The upper age limit is 30 years for UR/EWS candidates. Upper age relaxation of 5 years is granted to SC/ST (up to 35 years), 3 years for OBC-NCL (up to 33 years), up to 10-15 years for PwBD, and up to 20 years for retrenched ex-contingent MECL workmen.

faqs.question: Where will the MECL Written Examination and Skill Tests be conducted?
faqs.answer: All Written Competitive Examinations and subsequent Document Verification / Skill Tests will be conducted exclusively in Nagpur City (Maharashtra).

faqs.question: What is the weightage of the Written Examination in the selection process?
faqs.answer: The Written Examination carries 100% weightage. The Skill/Trade Test is purely of qualifying nature (Suitable or Not Suitable). The final merit list is drawn strictly based on Written Test marks.

faqs.question: What is the minimum qualifying percentage required in the Written Test?
faqs.answer: The minimum qualifying marks in the Written Examination are 50% for UR, OBC-NCL, and EWS candidates, and 45% for SC and ST candidates.

faqs.question: How many candidates will be called for Document Verification and Skill Test?
faqs.answer: Candidates clearing the written test cut-off will be called for Document Verification ordinarily in the ratio of 1:7 (7 candidates per advertised vacancy) in order of merit.

faqs.question: Is color blindness allowed for technical and driver posts in MECL?
faqs.answer: No. Absence of colour blindness and absence of night blindness is a mandatory medical requirement for Junior Driver (W-3), Mechanic (W-4), Mechanic-cum-Operator Drilling (W-4), Machinist (W-4), Technician Drilling (W-4), and Electrician (W-4).

faqs.question: Will MECL reimburse the medical examination fee?
faqs.answer: Yes, the fee incurred for the medical fitness examination by a Government Medical Officer or CMO will be reimbursed by MECL upon submission of the official receipt.

faqs.question: Does 1-year Apprenticeship training count as work experience for ITI candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes. As per Ministry of Skill Development OM dated 19.02.2024, 1 year of Apprenticeship Training with National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) under Schedule-1 is recognized as 1 year of post-qualification experience for ITI trade candidates.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for MECL Non-Executive recruitment?
faqs.answer: The application fee is Rs. 500/- for General (UR), OBC, and EWS candidates. SC, ST, PwBD, Ex-Servicemen, and internal MECL employees are completely exempted from payment of fees.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for more than one post under Advt 03/Rectt./2026?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates are allowed to apply for only one post as per their choice and eligibility. Multiple registrations for different posts are not permitted.

faqs.question: What pay scales and allowances are offered to MECL Non-Executive employees?
faqs.answer: Employees receive central public sector IDA pay scales: Grade W-7 (Rs. 22,900 - 55,900/-), Grade W-4 (Rs. 20,200 - 49,300/-), and Grade W-3 (Rs. 19,600 - 47,900/-), along with IDA, HRA, cafeteria perks, PRP incentives, medical cover, vehicle loans, and HBA.

faqs.question: What is the probation period in MECL?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates will be placed on probation for a minimum period of 1 year from the date of joining, extendable by up to 1 additional year based on performance.

faqs.question: Where will the selected candidates be posted?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates may be posted at MECL Corporate Office in Nagpur, or at any of MECL project sites, exploration camps, and establishments across India or overseas.

faqs.question: Do I need to send physical copies of the application form or certificates to MECL?
faqs.answer: No, applications are accepted exclusively online through www.mecl.co.in. Candidates should not send hard copies, but must retain a printed copy of the submitted form for Document Verification.

faqs.question: Where can candidates lodge technical grievances regarding the application portal?
faqs.answer: Candidates can contact the official helpdesk portal at https://cgrs.ibps.in/ during 09:30 AM to 06:00 PM on working days.

karnataka-public-service-group-a-b-recru.title: Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026 Notification Out for 319 Group 'A' & 'B' (KAS) Posts | Apply Online
overview: Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), 'Udyoga Soudha', Bengaluru has issued official notification No. KPSCKA/EXA1/EXMF/9/2026-EXAM-1/I/251710/2026 dated 31st July 2026 for the recruitment of 319 Gazetted Probationers (Group 'A' & Group 'B' - KAS) for the 2026-27 recruitment cycle under the Karnataka Recruitment of Gazetted Probationers (Appointment by Competitive Examinations) Rules. The recruitment encompasses 117 Group 'A' posts (including 39 Assistant Commissioners, 50 Assistant Commissioners of Commercial Taxes, 15 Executive Officers / Assistant Secretaries RDPR, 11 Assistant Directors Social Welfare) and 202 Group 'B' posts (including 74 Commercial Tax Officers, 25 Tahsildars Grade-2, 21 Assistant Registrars of Cooperative Societies, 20 Chief Officers Grade-1, 12 Assistant Treasury Officers, and other executive cadres).

Candidates holding a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree in any discipline from a recognized Indian University (or final year appearing candidates) are eligible to appear for the Preliminary Examination. The minimum age requirement is 21 years, and the maximum age limit is 40 years for General Merit, 43 years for Categories 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, and 45 years for SC, ST, and Category-1, factoring in the special one-time 5-year age concession granted vide Government Order No. DPAR 262 SeNeNi 2025 dated 29.01.2026. Special physical standards are prescribed for uniformed posts like Dy.SP, Assistant Superintendent (Prisons), and Deputy Superintendent of Excise.

The selection architecture features a rigorous three-tier evaluation: a Preliminary Examination (Objective Type: Paper 1 & Paper 2, 400 Marks, 1:15 ratio), followed by the Main Examination (Qualifying Kannada & English + 5 Compulsory Descriptive Papers, 1250 Marks), and an Oral Personality Test / Interview (25 Marks) for a combined final ranking out of 1275 Marks. Online applications can be submitted through the official portal at https://kpsconline.karnataka.gov.in. The preliminary examination is tentatively scheduled for 15 November 2026.

selectionProcess.description: Two objective papers (100 Qs / 200 Marks each, Total 400 Marks, 2 Hours each). Paper 1: General Studies National/International (80 M) + Humanities (120 M). Paper 2: General Studies State/Karnataka (80 M) + Science/Ecology (60 M) + Mental Ability (60 M). Negative marking of 0.25 marks. Shortlists candidates in 1:15 ratio for Mains.

Qualifying Papers (35% pass marks): Kannada (150 Marks) & English (150 Marks). Compulsory Merit Papers (250 Marks each / 3 Hours): Paper 1 Essay, Paper 2 GS-1, Paper 3 GS-2, Paper 4 GS-3, Paper 5 GS-4. Total Written Merit = 1250 Marks.
Personality evaluation carrying 25 Marks conducted by KPSC Selection Board (ratio 1:3). Focuses on leadership, decision making, analytical acumen, and civil service aptitude.
Verification of original degree, caste/income (Form D/E/F), Kannada Medium (KMS), Rural Certificate (Form 1/2), HK Article 371(J) certificate, and physical fitness test for uniformed posts.

reservation.title: Reservation Policy & Special Quota Provisions
detailsList: Hyderabad-Karnataka Region (Article 371-J): 22 posts exclusively reserved under HK local cadre across Group A and Group B.
Category-wise Reservations: SC (15%), ST (3%), Category-1 (4%), Category-2A (15%), Category-2B (4%), Category-3A (4%), Category-3B (5%).
Rural Reservation: 15% reservation for candidates who studied from 1st to 10th standard in rural schools (Form 1 & Form 2 required).
Kannada Medium Reservation (KMS): 5% reservation for candidates who studied 1st to 10th standard in Kannada medium.
Women Reservation: 33% horizontal reservation for women candidates across all categories.
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD): 4% horizontal reservation across identified cadres (Schedule-I to Schedule-VI of WCD notifications).
Ex-Servicemen Reservation: 10% horizontal reservation for released armed forces personnel.
Transgender Reservation: 1% horizontal reservation as per Karnataka State Civil Services Rules.

howToApply: Visit the official Karnataka Public Service Commission portal: https://kpsconline.karnataka.gov.in.
Complete One Time Registration (OTR) by providing Aadhaar/Kutumba ID, mobile number, and active email address.
Upload recent passport photograph (max 200 KB in JPG format) and clear signature (max 70 KB in JPG format).
Log in with your credentials, go to 'Active Notifications' and click 'Apply to Post' against Gazetted Probationers 2026-27 (Notification No. KPSCKA/EXA1/EXMF/9/2026-EXAM-1/I/251710/2026).
Select cadre preferences for Group A and Group B posts based on eligibility and interest.
Enter educational details, reservation categories (GM, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, SC, ST, HK 371J, Rural, Kannada Medium), and certificate RD numbers.
Pay the examination fee (₹600 for GM, ₹300 for 2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹50 for Ex-Mil) online via Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, or UPI.
Submit the online form before the extended deadline (07 September 2026) and verify the generated QR Code application receipt.

faqs.question: What is the educational qualification for KPSC Gazetted Probationers?
faqs.answer: Candidates must hold any Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree from a recognized university in India. Final year students appearing in qualifying degree exams are also eligible for the Preliminary exam.

faqs.question: What is the upper age limit for KPSC Gazetted Probationers 2026?

faqs.question: What is the selection process and exam pattern for KAS Gazetted Probationers?

overview: Medical and Health Recruitment Board (MHRB), Assam, operating under the Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Assam, has published official recruitment advertisement No. MHRB/73/M&HO-I/2026/5051 dated 3rd September 2026 inviting online applications from eligible Indian citizens for filling up 560 vacancies of Medical & Health Officer–I (M&HO-I) or its equivalent ranks. Selected candidates will be placed in the scale of pay of Rs. 30,000/- to Rs. 1,10,000/- with Grade Pay of Rs. 12,700/- plus admissible allowances under the Government of Assam Rules.

Candidates possessing an MBBS Degree from any recognized University under MCI (Medical Council of India / National Medical Commission) and valid registration under the Assam Medical Council (AMC) are eligible to apply. The age limit is 21 to 38 years as on 01 January 2026, with relaxation applicable for SC, STP, STH, OBC/MOBC, and PwBD candidates. Notably, serving doctors under DME, DHS, NHM Assam, and other state government agencies are eligible to apply without requiring a separate No Objection Certificate (NOC).

Online applications must be submitted via the official portal at https://nhm.assam.gov.in from 07 September 2026 until 20 September 2026. The application fee is Rs. 250/- for General candidates and Rs. 150/- for OBC/MOBC/SC/ST candidates, payable online through GRAS (https://assamegras.gov.in) or offline via Treasury Challan. PwBD candidates are fully exempted from application fees. The selection procedure (written test / viva-voce) will be notified by the Board based on the volume of applications received.

overview: High Court of Delhi has officially published the employment Vacancy Notice dated 02 September 2026 for the Senior Personal Assistant and Personal Assistant Examination 2026 to fill 150 existing Group 'B' Gazetted/Non-Gazetted vacancies and prepare a select panel thereof. The recruitment drive encompasses 117 vacancies for Senior Personal Assistant (SPA) in Pay Level 8 and 33 vacancies for Personal Assistant (PA) in Pay Level 7 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix.

Candidates possessing a Graduate Degree from a recognized University along with the prescribed English Shorthand and Typing benchmarks (SPA: 110 w.p.m. Shorthand & 40 w.p.m. Typing; PA: 100 w.p.m. Shorthand & 40 w.p.m. Typing on computer) and aged between 18 and 32 years as on 01 January 2026 are eligible to apply. Note that for the post of Personal Assistant (PA), vacancies are exclusively available for reserved categories (EWS: 7, OBC-NCL: 16, SC: 5, ST: 5), with NIL vacancies under the General category. Selected candidates will be posted in the High Court of Delhi, New Delhi, drawing competitive starting salaries of approx. ₹85,000 - ₹95,000/- for SPA and ₹80,000 - ₹90,000/- for PA.

The selection procedure involves a multi-tier assessment: Stage-I English Typing Test (40 w.p.m., Qualifying), Stage-II English Shorthand Test (110/100 w.p.m. transcription, 120/110 Marks), Stage-III Main Descriptive English Examination (Essay, Letter, Grammar, Translation - 100 Marks), and Stage-IV Interview (15 Marks). Online applications can be submitted on the official Delhi High Court portal (www.delhihighcourt.nic.in) from 15 September 2026 (11:00 AM) to 05 October 2026 (11:00 PM), with an application correction window available from 12 to 14 October 2026.

selectionProcess.description: 10 minutes duration on computers to assess minimum speed of 40 words per minute (w.p.m.) in English typing based on 'characters with space'. Maximum mistakes permissible: 3% of total words typed. Qualifying in nature; only qualifying candidates proceed to Stage-II.

For SPA: 110 w.p.m. dictation of 550 words in 5 minutes; 45 minutes computer transcription (120 Marks, max 5% / 27.5 mistakes permissible; 4 marks deducted per full mistake, 2 per half mistake). For PA: 100 w.p.m. dictation of 500 words in 5 minutes; 45 minutes transcription (110 Marks, max 5% / 25 mistakes permissible). Two shorthand tests given; best of two considered.

Descriptive English Test of 100 Marks (120 Minutes duration): Essay of 250 words (40 Marks), Letter Writing (15 Marks), Grammar & Comprehension Passage (25 Marks), and Translation (Hindi to English: 10 Marks & English to Hindi: 10 Marks). Minimum qualifying marks: General 50% (50/100), Reserved/PwBD 45% (45/100).

Interview of 15 Marks (no minimum qualifying cutoff). Final select merit list is prepared by aggregating marks from Stage-II (Shorthand Test), Stage-III (Descriptive Exam), and Stage-IV (Interview). Total Merit: 235 Marks for SPA, 225 Marks for PA.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official website of High Court of Delhi at https://delhihighcourt.nic.in/.
Step 2: Go to 'Public Notice' -> 'Recruitment - Job Openings' and click on 'Senior Personal Assistant and Personal Assistant Examination 2026'.
Step 3: Read the complete official Vacancy Notice carefully before proceeding with registration.
Step 4: Register online using an active Email ID and Mobile Number to receive system-generated Application Number and Password.
Step 5: Fill in the detailed online application form: personal details, category, educational qualifications, shorthand and typing speed declarations.
Step 6: Live Photograph Capture: Capture and upload a live photograph using your webcam/mobile camera in good lighting. Ensure face covers at least 75% of the photo area without cap/mask/spectacles.
Step 7: Upload scanned passport-size color photograph (100 KB to 200 KB, JPEG, not older than 3 months) which will be verified against the live photo.
Step 8: Upload scanned Left Hand Thumb Impression (50 KB to 200 KB) and Signature in running hand (50 KB to 150 KB, full name in capital letters is rejected).
Step 9: Pay the non-refundable examination fee online (₹1,500/- for Gen/OBC/EWS; ₹1,300/- for SC/ST/PwBD) through UPI, Net Banking, or Credit/Debit Card on or before 05 October 2026 (11:00 PM).
Step 10: Submit the form and download/print the Confirmation Page. (Correction window will be open from 12 to 14 October 2026 with applicable charges).

overview: Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA), Bengaluru, in coordination with the Department of School Education (Pre-University), Government of Karnataka, has officially released employment advertisement notifications No. ED/KEA/28/Recruitment/2026 (RPC) and ED/KEA/29/Recruitment/2026 (KK) dated 03 September 2026 for the recruitment of 247 Group 'A' Principal (ಪ್ರಾಂಶುಪಾಲರು) vacancies under the Direct Recruitment Quota in Government Pre-University Colleges across the state.

The recruitment encompasses 216 vacancies in the Residual Parent Cadre (RPC) and 31 vacancies in the Kalyana-Karnataka (KK / Article 371-J) Local Cadre. In accordance with state recruitment rules, 100% of these Group 'A' Principal direct recruitment posts are to be filled from eligible in-service Lecturers working across various disciplines in Government Pre-University Colleges who have completed at least 10 years of service and satisfactorily completed their probationary period. Since the posts are filled exclusively from serving government lecturers, there is NO upper age limit (ವಯೋಮಿತಿಯ ಮಿತಿ ಇರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ). Selected candidates will be appointed in the 2024 Revised Karnataka State Pay Scale of ₹90,200 - ₹1,59,200/-.

Candidates will be selected through a state-level Competitive Examination comprising three objective MCQ papers (Paper 1: Kannada Language [Qualifying, min 50 marks required], Paper 2: General Studies [150 Marks], and Paper 3: Service Rules, Administration & Education [150 Marks]). Merit ranking will be determined strictly on the combined aggregate score of Paper 2 and Paper 3 (Total 300 Marks), followed by Document Verification in a 1:2 ratio. The online application portal opens on 07 September 2026 and closes on 04 October 2026 at https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) website at https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/.
Step 2: Navigate to the 'Recruitment' section and select 'Department of School Education (Pre-University) - Recruitment of Principals 2026'.

Step 4: Click on 'Online Application Form' and complete the One Time Registration (OTR) / Login using your mobile number and email ID.
Step 5: Fill in your personal details, academic qualifications, and complete in-service lecturer teaching experience details.
Step 6: Upload the prescribed Service Certificate (ಸೇವಾ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರ) duly signed by your Principal / Head of Office.
Step 7: Upload recent passport size photograph (JPEG/JPG, 50 KB to 200 KB) and signature (JPEG/JPG, 50 KB to 70 KB) in black ink.
Step 8: Upload caste/category (Form D/E/F/H), rural, Kannada medium, and 371(J) certificates with valid RD numbers where applicable.
Step 9: Pay the required application fee online through Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI on or before 05 October 2026.
Step 10: Verify all entered details, submit the application form, and download/print the final confirmation page for future reference.

up-anganwadi-anganwadi-karyakartri-angan.applicationStatus: Online Applications Open 04 September 2026 to 24 September 2026
overview: Office of the District Programme Officer, Amroha, Uttar Pradesh (कार्यालय : जिला कार्यक्रम अधिकारी, अमरोहा) has officially released employment advertisement notification No. C-671 / जि०का०अधि० / बा०वि०परि० / विज्ञप्ति / 2026-27 dated 03 September 2026 in accordance with UP Government Order No. 1/1092245/2025/3313/58-1-2025 (197687) dated 17 September 2025. Online applications are invited on http://upanganwadibharti.in for the direct recruitment of 105 vacancies for the honorarium-based post of Anganwadi Karyakatri (आंगनबाड़ी कार्यकत्री / Worker) across seven child development projects in Amroha district.

The 105 vacancies are distributed across Amroha Shahar (Urban - 10), Amroha Dehat (Rural - 9), Dhanaura (Rural - 26), Gajraula (Rural - 17), Gangeshwari (Rural - 6), Hasanpur (Rural - 12), and Joya (Rural - 25). Only female candidates who are permanent residents of the concerned Gram Sabha / Ward (or Nyaya Panchayat if no eligible candidate is available in the Gram Sabha) and aged between 18 and 35 years as on 01 July 2026 are eligible. Applicants must have passed at least Intermediate (10+2 / 12th Pass) or equivalent from a recognized board; higher educational qualifications up to Post Graduation will be credited during academic merit preparation.

Selection is conducted purely on a 100% Merit Basis calculated from academic percentages (Class 10th to Post Graduation) and statutory residency/category priorities. There is NO written examination and NO interview. Priority is accorded to Below Poverty Line (BPL) Widows, legally divorced, and deserted women of the same village/ward. Online applications must be submitted on http://upanganwadibharti.in starting from 04 September 2026 until 24 September 2026 (up to 12:00 Midnight). Offline applications are strictly barred.

reservation.title: Reservation & Priority Guidelines for UP Anganwadi Recruitment
detailsList: Gender Exclusivity: 100% of posts are reserved exclusively for female candidates (केवल महिला अभ्यर्थी ही पात्र होंगी).
First Priority: Widow (विधवा), legally divorced (तलाकशुदा), or deserted (परित्यक्ता) women living below the poverty line (BPL) belonging to the same Gram Sabha / Ward.
Second Priority: Above Poverty Line (APL) widow, legally divorced, or deserted women belonging to the same village/ward in case BPL applicants are unavailable.
Third Priority: General eligible female candidates residing in the same village/ward selected in order of academic merit points.
BPL Income Threshold: Annual household income must not exceed ₹46,080/- for rural candidates and ₹56,460/- for urban candidates (as per GO No. 22/2015/2123/26-2-2015 dated 14.09.2015).
Income Certificate: Must be issued by the Competent Tehsildar with online digital verification capability (as per Revenue Dept GO No. 3959/1-9-11-रा०-9 dated 30.09.2021).
Single-Family Restriction: Two women from the same family cannot be appointed as Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper at the same Anganwadi Center.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official UP Anganwadi recruitment portal at http://upanganwadibharti.in.

Step 2: On the homepage, choose District as 'Amroha', select your Child Development Project (Amroha Shahar, Amroha Dehat, Dhanaura, Gajraula, Gangeshwari, Hasanpur, or Joya), and select your Gram Sabha or Ward.
Step 3: Read the official advertisement (पत्रांक: C-671/जि०का०अधि०/बा०वि०परि०/विज्ञप्ति/2026-27 dated 03.09.2026) and eligibility instructions thoroughly.
Step 4: Click on 'Register' and enter your active Mobile Number and Aadhaar details to generate your registration number and password.
Step 5: Fill in your personal details, guardian/husband name, date of birth, category, and marital status (Widow/Divorced/General).
Step 6: Enter your educational qualifications (High School, Intermediate, Graduation, Post Graduation) with exact roll numbers, marks obtained, and maximum marks.
Step 7: Upload self-attested scanned copies of educational marksheets, digital domicile certificate with ward/village details, income certificate, and caste certificate.
Step 8: Upload recent passport size photograph and signature in clear readable format.
Step 9: Thoroughly review all entered details in the application preview window; offline or post-submission changes will not be permitted.
Step 10: Submit the application online before the deadline of 24 September 2026 (12:00 Midnight) and download/print the final application confirmation slip.
documentsRequired: High School (Class 10th) Marksheet and Certificate for Date of Birth proof
Intermediate (Class 12th) Marksheet and Certificate (essential minimum qualification)
Graduation and Post Graduation Marksheets and Degree Certificates (if applicable for merit score)
Digitally signed Online Domicile Certificate (निवास प्रमाण पत्र) issued by Tehsil showing Ward Name/Number (Urban) or Gram Sabha (Rural)
Digitally signed Online Income Certificate (आय प्रमाण पत्र) issued by Tehsil certifying BPL income (below ₹46,080/- Rural or ₹56,460/- Urban)
Digitally signed Online Caste Certificate (जाति प्रमाण पत्र) for SC/ST/OBC categories issued by Tehsil
Death Certificate of husband and certified copy of Family Register (परिवार पंजिका नकल) from Panchayat/Municipality for Widow applicants
Certified Court Decree / Legal Order for Divorced or Deserted women claiming priority
Recent passport size color photograph of the candidate
Candidate's signature in clear black ink
Aadhaar Card or Government Photo ID Proof
importantInstructions: Only female candidates who are permanent residents of the concerned Gram Sabha / Ward are eligible to apply.
Age must be between 18 and 35 years as on 01 July 2026. Age will be strictly verified from the High School certificate.
No offline application will be accepted under any circumstances. All applications must be submitted online on http://upanganwadibharti.in.
All uploaded certificates must be self-attested, clean, and clearly legible. Illegible or forged documents will lead to summary rejection and legal proceedings.
Annual income certificates must be verifiable online through the UP eDistrict portal.
Two women from the same household cannot be appointed at the same Anganwadi Center.
The closing date for online submission is 24 September 2026 (till 12:00 midnight).

The application window is open from 05 September 2026 (10:30 AM) to 18 September 2026 (05:00 PM) on all working days. Candidates can view official updates on the Nandyal District official portal at nandyal.ap.gov.in.

The recruitment is specifically conducted for eligible enrolled and trained Home Guards (including daily duty allowance sports personnel) possessing a graduate degree and minimum 5 years of duty experience.

Selected candidates will be appointed in Pay Level-6 with attractive state allowances, medical benefits, and structured career progression as gazetted supervisory officers in Bihar Home Guard. The selection process consists of two-stage objective written competitive examination (Preliminary Examination of 200 marks and Main Examination comprising General Hindi and General Studies of 200 marks each, with 0.2 negative marking), followed by Physical Efficiency Test (PET), Physical Standard Test (PST), medical examination, and character verification. Final merit list is framed strictly on the basis of marks scored in Main Written Examination Paper-2.

Online applications must be submitted via the official BPSSC portal at bpssc.bihar.gov.in under the 'Home Guard' tab. The online application window commences on 10 September 2026 and closes on 10 October 2026. All categories of applicants (Male, Female, and Third Gender) are required to pay a uniform application fee of Rs. 100/- online.

howToApply: Visit the official website of Bihar Police Subordinate Services Commission at https://bpssc.bihar.gov.in.
Navigate to the 'Home Guard' tab and click on the link for 'Advt. No. 11/2026 - Apply Online for Gulma Samadesta (Company Commander)'.

Step 1 (Registration & Fee Payment): Fill in candidate name, nationality, mobile number, email ID, Bihar domicile, reservation category, gender, and date of birth. Pay the online application fee of Rs. 100/-.
Receive Registration Number and Password on registered mobile SMS and email.

Step 2 (Application Form): Log in using credentials and enter father/husband name, mother name, permanent & correspondence address, educational qualifications (Graduation details), and Bihar Home Guard service/training certificate details.

Upload scanned color photograph (white background, taken within 2 months, 15-25 KB, .jpg/.jpeg/.gif format) and scanned signatures in Hindi and English (black or blue ink, 15-25 KB, white background).
Review all entries using the 'Edit Details' button before final submission. Click 'Submit' to finalize the application.
Download and print the Confirmation Page / Acknowledgement Slip on A4 size paper for document verification and future reference.
